before: video and audio embed media. The controls attribute asks the browser to show playback controls.

A source element names a media file and can state its type.
```html
<audio controls>
  <source src="birds.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
</audio>
```
The file must exist and be supported; markup alone does not supply a recording.

A track element can attach timed captions to video. Captions include meaningful sounds as well as speech.
```html
<track kind="captions" src="birds-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
```
WebVTT is a text format for timed cues. Matching src, language and label is not proof that captions are accurate or synchronized.
A transcript gives another way to read the information. Keep its link outside the media element so it remains available even when the browser supports the player but cannot load the recording.
Fallback text inside audio or video is for browsers that do not support that element; it is not a reliable error message for every media-loading failure.
For this practice, file names are example references. The checks inspect structure; they do not download, play, transcribe or verify media.
